```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's lake example (its `lake_ex` vignette), whose data are simulated
based on Francis et al. (2011, *Ecology Letters*, doi:10.1111/j.1461-0248.2011.01597.x): zooplankton in 21
lakes, two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) and three sources (terrestrial detritus, surface
particulate organic matter (POM) and subsurface POM). The diet changes along a
continuous effect, each lake's ratio of Secchi depth to mixing depth
(`Secchi.Mixed`), a measure of how far light reaches into the mixed layer. The source
data are raw samples, and the error structure is Residual only. Only the fitting call
differs from MixSIAR's: `run_pfn()` in place of `write_JAGS_model()` and
`run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "lake_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = NULL, fac_random = NULL,
  fac_nested = NULL, cont_effects = "Secchi.Mixed")
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "lake_sources.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "raw", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "lake_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
```

`load_source_data()` summarises the raw source samples to each source's mean, SD and
sample size, which is what MixSIARPFN's networks use:

```{r sources, eval = TRUE}
source$data
```

There are `r mix$N` lakes (one consumer row each), with `Secchi.Mixed` from
`r num(min(mix$data$Secchi.Mixed))` to `r num(max(mix$data$Secchi.Mixed))`.

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual only error and MixSIAR's uninformative Dirichlet prior, as in MixSIAR's
vignette.

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = FALSE)
)
fit
```

## Results

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

The diet along `Secchi.Mixed`, as in MixSIAR's vignette:

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
for (p in out$plots[grepl("Secchi", names(out$plots))]) print(p)
```

```{r trend, include = FALSE}
cs <- fit$summary[fit$summary$block == "Secchi.Mixed (continuous)", ]
cs$x <- as.numeric(cs$level)
ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cs, cs$source), function(d) data.frame(
  source = d$source[1], low = d$mean[which.min(d$x)], high = d$mean[which.max(d$x)])))
up <- ends[which.max(ends$high - ends$low), ]
down <- ends[which.min(ends$high - ends$low), ]
```

From the lowest to the highest `Secchi.Mixed`, the share of `r if (ok) up$source` rises
from `r num(up$low)` to `r num(up$high)` and the share of `r if (ok) down$source` falls
from `r num(down$low)` to `r num(down$high)`.

## Comparison with MixSIAR

```{r reference}
ref <- mixsiar_reference("lake")
ref_raw <- mixsiar_reference("lake_raw")
blocks <- character(0)
```

With a continuous effect, each consumer has its own diet. Each lake's diet from
MixSIARPFN against MixSIAR's (MixSIAR's `p.ind`), along `Secchi.Mixed`:

```{r covariate, fig.height = 4}
plot_compare_covariate(fit, ref$pind)
```

```{r cov-numbers, include = FALSE}
pf <- merge(fit$consumers[, c("consumer", "level")],
            fit$summary[fit$summary$block == "consumer", c("level", "source", "mean")], by = "level")
pc <- merge(pf, ref$pind[, c("consumer", "source", "mean")], by = c("consumer", "source"),
            suffixes = c("_pfn", "_mixsiar"))
cov_gap <- mean(abs(pc$mean_pfn - pc$mean_mixsiar))
```

The two curves follow each other closely: the consumers' posterior mean diets differ
by `r num(cov_gap, 3)` on average.

The global diet (at the average `Secchi.Mixed`) and the residual multipliers:
